text.p: Bonds ended slightly lower in a session of low volatility with the market discounting a 0.25 percentage point rise in the U.S. discount rate on Tuesday, traders said.
The market is not expecting the Bank of Portugal to cut its repurchase or drain rates on Tuesday at the start of a new commercial bank reserve period.

But the calm with which the market was waiting for the Federal Reserve rate decision was broken by a warning from Bundesbank Council member Ernst Welteke that a U.S. rise could push German rates up as well.
Traders said that on Tuesday the market would mark time, waiting for the Fed and watching the movements in other periphery markets.
"The question is the nervousness expressed by the Buba (Welteke). This is the unknown that is making everybody cautious," said one trader.
Any rate rise by Germany would clearly cut Portugal's room to reduce, they said.
